reason: The lens needs a holder that can slide to adjust focus.
expectation: The lens will fit into the adjustable holder.

effect: The lens is now in an adjustable assembly, ready to fit to the theatre.
reason: The theatre needs the adjustable lens to project and focus the star pattern.
expectation: The lens assembly will attach in front of the star wheel.

effect: The lens is installed, and its slider can be used to compare focus once the cloth is hung.
reason: The projector is ready for its screen, so the hanging cloth is the natural next piece.
expectation: The cloth will provide a screen for the projected stars.

effect: The cloth provides a screen, and sliding the lens brings the star-disc image into focus.
reaction: The explanation made the focusing step clear.
reason: The lens hood should help shield the projection from stray light.
expectation: The hood will attach around the lens.

alternatives.reason: The handle will also be needed to turn the star wheel.

effect: The hood reduces stray light and makes the projected stars stand out; the wheel still needs a way to turn.
reaction: The contrast improvement makes the hood's purpose clear.
reason: The star-wheel handle should let the focused sky turn.
expectation: The handle will turn the star wheel and move the projected stars.

effect: The handle completed the star theatre: turning the wheel moves the projected stars, and the image is inverted.
reaction: The upside-down image was a surprising detail, and the drifting stars brought the pieces together nicely.

mostWorthwhile.text: Focusing the star image was most worthwhile: sliding the lens connected the adjustment to a visible change and explained how the projector forms an image.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the lens into its holder was straightforward preparation, though it was necessary for the projector.

surprise.text: The projected image turned out upside down, an unexpected feature of the finished theatre.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the hood's effect on contrast clarified why it was there.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the projector and the earlier inventions fit into the fair, especially after the final scene linked them to Jo's drawing.
